title: OpenAI ChatCompletions compact request/response mapper and streaming coercer
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a compact, low-latency compatibility layer that maps OpenAI Chat Completions (v1/chat/completions) request and response shapes into Redwood's canonical streaming + tool-calling + structured-output pipeline. This ticket focuses on a lightweight proxy that: 1) accepts legacy OA ChatCompletion requests, 2) performs deterministic request reshaping (roles, content chunks, top-level params), 3) initiates Redwood's streaming runtime with tool-call hooks and structured output enforcement, and 4) remaps the streamed events back into an OpenAI-compatible response envelope so legacy clients remain unchanged. Background: We have many customers using OA-compatible SDKs and third-party middleware that expect the ChatCompletions wire shape and SSE streaming chunks. Full-featured compatibility layers exist in other tickets, but they are heavy. This work is a minimal, well-instrumented shim intended for quick rollout to reduce customer friction while we evolve the richer adapter. Constraints: - No persistent schema translation state between requests. - Must preserve idempotency keys and session metadata when present. - Must enforce structured output contracts for function/tool calling responses. - Must limit added latency to <15ms median at p50 for small requests on dedicated capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OA ChatCompletions payloads and returns 200 + stream-compatible SSE frames to legacy clients
Tool/function calls invoked by models are surfaced to Redwood's tool invocation layer and returned as OA-compatible function_call messages
Structured-output responses (JSON schema) are validated against provided schema hints; failures produce a clear OA-style "function_call"/message with validation diagnostics
End-to-end tests demonstrating idempotent replay for identical request IDs (x-request-id) pass
Latency regression <5% at p50 in canary region compared to direct Redwood API calls (same model)
implementation_notes: Add a compact request normalizer module that: maps 'messages' role/content to internal prompt Blocks, flattens assistant/system roles, preserves 'max_tokens', 'temperature', 'top_p' as runtime flags
Implement streaming output marshaller: translate internal token events / function_call events into OA SSE 'data: {"id":..., "choices":[...] }' envelope with 'delta' fragments
Toolcall mapping: internal tool invocation -> OA 'function_call' object with 'name' and serialized 'arguments' field; return path rehydrates native tool outputs into assistant messages
Error mapping: map internal retryable errors to OA 5xx conventions and include 'error' field compatible with client SDKs
Expose a feature-flag gate and 'compat-mode' header for canarying per-customer
Place the shim as a thin HTTP reverse-proxy in front of the runtime ingress; avoid touching core runtime code paths to minimize blast radius
mapping_examples:
Request mapping example: OA payload -> Redwood normalized string:
{
  "model": "gpt-4-mini",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Summarize quarterly goals"}],
  "temperature": 0.2
}
becomes:
PROMPT_BLOCK: [SYSTEM: "redwood-canonical-system"] + USER: "Summarize quarterly goals" | FLAGS: temperature=0.2

Streaming response example (SSE chunk): internal event -> OA SSE chunk:
data: {"id":"r-760821","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"In Q1 we"}, "index":0, "finish_reason":null}]}
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal canary behind feature-flag for engineering teams (1 day)
Phase B: opt-in beta for select customers (2 days) - monitor telemetry & support logs
Phase C: gradual 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic ramp over a week with auto-rollback on SLO regressions
Fallback: if structured-output failures exceed threshold, route requests to non-compat direct endpoint and emit incident alert
test_plan: Unit tests: request normalizer, SSE marshaller, function_call serializer/deserialize
Integration tests: end-to-end OA request to tool invocation to assistant response using mocked tool endpoints
Load tests: 1k concurrent small requests to ensure median added latency <15ms
Compatibility tests: run community OA client suites (node/python) against shim and verify behavior matches baseline
telemetry: Emit 'compat.shim.latency' histogram (ms) with tags: model, region, customer_id
Create Grafana dashboard comparing compat vs native runtime p50/p95 latencies and error rates
